rows.grounds: bahuvrīhi compound qualifying bījam; nāda and bindu as constituents
past passive participle stating the prescribed form

items.question: What specific form is declared as the seed-syllable of āsurī?
premises: A seed-syllable is the subject being specified.
The seed-syllable is characterized as endowed with nāda and bindu.
This characterization is fully declared as authoritative.
items.inference: The seed-syllable of āsurī is declared to be endowed with nāda and bindu.
items.plain_english: The seed-syllable of āsurī is declared to be endowed with nāda and bindu.
